summary: PASS 1 grind (2026-08-04): re-measured the prototype's own source (design/prototype/Clio Session.html) directly rather than trusting this file's prior text. Two real findings changed the plan: (1) kit/Layer.tsx's own #331 doc comment already said files/artifacts/ctx are OVERLAYS, not right-pane content — but an intervening owner-review-1 pass had routed all three into the AppShell right-hand `detail` slot anyway, which is a real deviation from the measured prototype (`layerFiles: true` opens a centered LayerChrome window; `tgArtifacts`/`tgTelemetry` both set `layerObs: true` and just switch `obsTab`, never opening a panel of their own). Fixed: files now opens as its own modal Layer (tree + preview + attach + honestly-degraded browse/save); artifacts/ctx pills now deep-link into the SAME Observability layer the eye icon opens, on the matching tab. (2) The Observability 'context' tab was a bare 2-row KvGrid; it now renders the measured progress-bar+hero, a 3-tile row (relay latency / thinking tokens / cost), and an orange 'live now' box built from the SAME `runs` data the runs tab already has — relay latency and thinking-token counts have no wire source anywhere in the app and are rendered as an honest 'not reported' tile rather than fabricated; cost is real (summed message `cost_usd`). Console dock and its desktop-only gate were already correct going into this pass (owner-review-1) and are unchanged. The Detail Slot's CHROME (kind badge, breadcrumb, copy/download, maximize) is now built, but its REACHABILITY from the live transcript remains a wire gap tracked separately as E7 — nothing in the transcript opens it yet, only the `?shell` fixture harness.

items.element: Files Layer content — tree sidebar + file preview + attach-to-message
items.proto_truth: Modal window (LayerChrome, width×height=winW×winH, 8vh top margin): header folder-icon + 'files' + path meta (fsRootPath) + 'browse…' button + maximize/pop-out/close; body = resizable tree column (filter input, chevron/folder rows, size right-aligned e.g. '48 KB') + right content pane showing selected file path, raw content, 'ATTACH TO MESSAGE' button, and a 'SAVE' button. Re-measured directly from design/prototype/Clio Session.html: winW=680 (default), winH=72vh, bpTreeW=210; on-browse/on-close are the LayerChrome props (no on-maximize/on-popout prop is passed for the files/blueprint/provider-config layers — only Observability's own markup has window controls, so this window correctly has no maximize/pop-out either).
items.audit_correction: Downgraded match -> deviates by the independent audit (2026-08-04): the live wire's GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/files returns entries typed `"dir"` (probed directly against 127.0.0.1:17900), but FilesLayer.tsx:59,64 classifies with `file.type !== 'directory'` — `'dir' !== 'directory'` is always true, so every leaf dir entry is misclassified as a FILE. Visually confirmed on screenshots/side-by-side/audit-files.png: repo directories (.claude, .clio-relay, .clio-child-cache, …) render as flat doc-icon 'file' rows with no folder chevron/grouping at the root, while the prototype pane shows chevroned folders. The unit tests pass because their fixtures never use the wire's actual `type:'dir'` spelling — a prove-the-invariant-on-the-real-object miss. Fix: treat `'dir'` (and `'directory'`) as directory in FilesLayer.buildFileTree.
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/session/FilesLayer.tsx — real folder tree grouped client-side from the flat backend listing (buildFileTree), chevron expand/collapse (root level open by default, deeper levels closed, filtering force-opens ancestors of a match), filter input, size column, and a preview pane with a WORKING 'attach to message' (inserts `@path` into the composer draft — the prototype's own button has no click handler at all, a static mockup element, so this is a functional improvement) and an honestly-degraded, permanently-disabled 'save' (no workspace file-write endpoint exists) and 'browse…' (no filesystem traversal above the registered workspace root exists). Tests: tests/unit/panels-conformance.test.tsx ('files layer' describe blocks, 5 tests) + tests/unit/owner-review-1.test.tsx. Composite: panels-files.png. Not built: the drag-to-resize corner handle (dragWin) — cosmetic, not requested by this item's acceptance.
items.backend_surface: GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/files, GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/files/read — consumed. No write/save endpoint and no filesystem-traversal-above-root endpoint exist — both wire gaps, both visibly marked (data-unbacked, disabled, explanatory title), never silently omitted.

Click opens apps/web/src/session/ConsoleDock.tsx via SessionView's dock prop (panel==='console'). Re-verified by source read this pass; tests/unit/owner-review-1.test.tsx exercises the open+close.

items.proto_truth: Resizable dock anchored to the bottom of the center column (not a right/side panel): tab bar ('bash' + '+' new-shell + per-tab close), drag-to-resize handle, REPL body with cyan prompt (e.g. 'j4471@ares:j4471$'), command echo, gray output, live input line.
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/session/ConsoleDock.tsx — dock anchored via AppShell's `dock` slot below the center column (not a side panel), tab pill ('bash' + disabled '+' new-console), resize-handle strip, a cyan '$' prompt line, and an explicit, honest unbacked marker (data-unbacked='true') explaining no session shell/PTY wire surface exists — the correct degraded behavior, not a gap to hide. Unchanged this pass (already correct from owner-review-1); re-verified by source read only — a fresh visual composite could NOT be generated this pass (see notes/wire gaps: the side-by-side script's console setup spoofs window.isTauri without a real Tauri bridge, which crashes the app's tauriFetch-routed boot probe). The prompt reads a generic '$' rather than a realistic 'user@host:path$' — a minor remaining content gap.
items.fix_hint: Follow-up, not this pass: side-by-side.mjs's console setup needs a real (or stubbed) Tauri invoke bridge before window.isTauri=true can be spoofed safely — right now it crashes ALL backend fetches once the flag is set (apps/web/src/backend/connection.ts routes fetch through tauriFetch whenever inTauri() is true), which the connect/probe flow swallows into an 'unreachable' failure. Worth a dedicated tooling fix, and also worth giving ConsoleDock a placeholder prompt string closer to the prototype's own.

items.proto_truth: Rich panel (walk-ctx-panel.png / proto-obs-context.png): a filled progress bar labelled 'context window' with '82.1k / 200k · 41%'; three stat tiles — RELAY LATENCY '12 ms' / 'clio-relay (ares)', THINKING TOKENS '600' / '2 blocks', COST '$0.31' / 'incl. subagents'; an orange-bordered 'LIVE NOW · 3' box listing live async jobs (e.g. 'stripe-tuner · getstripe 6,143/9,800 · 12.4k tok ↑').
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/observability/Observability.tsx's ContextTab now renders the same grammar: a 'context window' label + '{tokens} / {limit} · {percent}%' row, a filled progress bar, a 3-tile row (RELAY LATENCY / THINKING TOKENS / COST), and an orange-bordered 'live now · N' box built from the SAME `runs` array the runs tab already shows (filtered to non-terminal states) — no separate fetch. Composite: panels-context.png, near-pixel match on chrome. Tests: tests/unit/panels-conformance.test.tsx ('observability context tab' describe, 4 tests).
items.backend_surface: fetchSessionContextState supplies usedPercent/tokens/limit (unchanged). COST is now real — summed `cost_usd` across the session's messages (a real per-message wire field), shown only when at least one message actually reported one. RELAY LATENCY and THINKING TOKENS have NO wire source anywhere in the app (grepped the whole wire/client layer) — rendered as an explicit 'not reported' tile (data-unbacked='true') rather than fabricated or silently dropped. Per-job progress fractions and token throughput in the live-now box (e.g. '6,143/9,800 · 12.4k tok ↑') are similarly unbacked — ObsRun only carries label/agent/state/host/duration, so the live-now rows show those four fields honestly rather than invented numbers.
items.fix_hint: If/when a relay-latency or thinking-token-count wire field ships, wire it into ObsContext the same way costUsd was added; per-job live throughput would need ObsRun extended with real progress/token fields from the backend, not estimated client-side.

Default width 480px (`s.rightW || 480`), border-left, flex:0 0 auto — a true right-hand pane, distinct from the files/console/artifacts/ctx overlay layers (which are now correctly NOT using this slot — see above).

Tracked as backlog item E7 ('mint real artifacts and ground the chips'); not attempted this pass per that item's own scope boundary.

items.element: Detail slot chrome (kind badge, breadcrumb, copy/download, maximize, collapse-to-rail)
items.proto_truth: Header row: uppercase colored kind badge (e.g. 'ARTIFACT'); for artifact kind, a copy-markdown icon button and a download icon button (opens a menu: 'download file' / 'open storage location' / 'copy link to artifact'); a Maximize button (detExpand, grows to a centered 1120px-max modal with scrim); a 'Collapse panel' icon button (tgRight); a Close (×) button. Below: clickable breadcrumb trail (crumbs, e.g. 'session > earthscope_stations_…'). For artifact kind, a 3-way segmented sub-tab row labelled ARTIFACT / PROVENANCE / RECREATE.
items.app_evidence: apps/web/src/detail/DetailSlot.tsx rebuilt: uppercase kind badge (Chip, defaults 'ARTIFACT' via a new ArtifactRecord.recordKind field), a working copy-as-markdown button (real clipboard write of id/kind/size/sha/note — the download menu items have no backend equivalent so only a plain download affordance is offered, degraded/disabled with an explanatory title), a Maximize button that reopens the SAME content inside a centered <Layer width=1120> and restores on close, and a breadcrumb row (ArtifactRecord.breadcrumb, rendered only when the caller supplies one — nothing does yet, see the reachability item above). First tab renamed 'overview' → 'artifact'. Tests: tests/unit/detail.test.tsx (+7 new). NOT built: the download menu's 3 sub-items (no per-item backend action exists, so a single degraded button stands in rather than a fake menu with 3 fake actions), and 'Collapse panel' as a DISTINCT action from Close (no thin-rail collapsed state exists anywhere in AppShell to collapse into — building a second button that behaves identically to Close would be decorative, not a real feature, so it was left out honestly rather than faked).
items.backend_surface: n/a (chrome + content-rendering gap, independent of the reachability wiring gap above). No file-download endpoint exists — the download button is visibly degraded (data-unbacked, disabled, title) via a new ToolbarButton `unbacked` prop, matching the composer-attach-button convention.
items.fix_hint: Once E7 makes this reachable: add the download menu's 3 real actions if/when backed, and design a real collapsed-rail state on AppShell before adding a genuine 'collapse panel' control.
